fcr_pigs.unit: kg feed per kg liveweight gain
fcr_pigs.what: FCR on liveweight gain, commercial pigs UK/Europe 2011: about 1 as piglets rising to about 3 at slaughter (US 2012: 3.46 at 240-250 lb, i.e. the marginal FCR of the last weight band). Feed as fed, not stated as dry matter.
fcr_pigs.quote: As of 2011, pigs used commercially in the UK and Europe had an FCR, calculated using weight gain, of about 1 as piglets and ending about 3 at time of slaughter.

fcr_broilers.what: US broiler industry average 2025, feed per unit liveweight (1.91-1.92 in 2011; world average 2013 about 2.0 liveweight / 2.8 carcass per Wikipedia FCR article citing FAO).
fcr_broilers.quote: Table row (Year / Market Age days / Market Weight lb liveweight / Feed to Meat Gain, pounds of feed to one pound of broiler, liveweight / Mortality %): 2025 47.5 6.63 1.70 5.95

fcr_layers.what: FCR of US laying hens 2011, feed mass per mass of eggs (OWID/Alexander et al. 2016 gives 2.3 for eggs).
fcr_layers.quote: For hens used in egg production in the US, as of 2011 the FCR was about 2, with each hen laying about 330 eggs per year.

fcr_beef.unit: kg feed per kg liveweight gain
fcr_beef.what: US beef cattle 2013, FCR on liveweight gain, normal range; above 6 typical; carcass-weight FCR above 10. Page does not say dry matter explicitly (source is a feed-efficiency talk where intake is normally DM). Whole-system figure per kg edible product is far higher: OWID/Alexander 2016 gives 25.
fcr_beef.quote: As of 2013 in the US, an FCR calculated on live weight gain of 4.5–7.5 was in the normal range with an FCR above 6 being typical. Divided by an average carcass yield of 62.2%, the typical carcass weight FCR is above 10.

fcr_sheep.unit: kg feed dry matter per kg liveweight gain
fcr_sheep.what: Lambs on high-concentrate rations; 5 to 6 on good-quality forage.
fcr_sheep.quote: An FCR (kg feed dry matter intake per kg live mass gain) for lambs is often in the range of about 4 to 5 on high-concentrate rations, 5 to 6 on some forages of good quality

fcr_fish.what: Farmed fish FCR on whole live fish: Atlantic salmon ~1 (2015), tilapia ~1.5, catfish ~1 (2013). Edible-fillet FCR: tilapia ~4.6, Chinese carp ~4.9.
fcr_fish.quote: As of 2015 farm-raised Atlantic salmon had a commodified feed supply with four main suppliers, and an FCR of around 1. Tilapia is about 1.5, and as of 2013 farmed catfish had an FCR of about 1. [...] The edible (fillet) FCR of tilapia is around 4.6 and the FCR of Chinese carp is around 4.9.

feed_per_kg_milk.unit: kg feed per kg whole milk
feed_per_kg_milk.what: Feed required per kg of whole milk, OWID chart 'Feed required to produce one kilogram of meat or dairy product' (data: Alexander et al. 2016; the dry-matter basis is my reading of that dataset, not printed in the CSV). Corroboration: Wikipedia FCR article says dairy feed efficiency (milk/intake by weight) of 1.30-1.70 is normal, i.e. 0.59-0.77 kg feed per kg milk.
feed_per_kg_milk.quote: CSV row: Whole Milk,2013,0.7 (column feed_conversion_ratio__alexander_et_al__2016); same file: Beef 25, Lamb/mutton 15, Pork 6.4, Poultry 3.3, Eggs 2.3

milk_per_cow.unit: kg milk per cow per year
milk_per_cow.what: Cow milk yield per cow per year: India 1,154 kg (2010, low), USA 9,954 kg (2010), Israel 12,546 kg (highest, FAO survey 2001-2007). World average across ALL milk animals (cows, buffalo, goats, sheep) 2024 = 1,161 kg/animal/yr and USA 10,680 (OWID grapher milk-yields-per-animal, rows 'World,OWID_WRL,2024,1160.9434' and 'United States,USA,2024,10679.531').
milk_per_cow.quote: FAO reports Israel dairy farms are the most productive in the world, with a yield of 12,546 kg milk per cow per year. [...] The milk yield per cow in the United States was 9,954 kg per year in 2010. In contrast, the milk yields per cow in India and China – the second and third largest producers – were respectively 1,154 kg and 2,282 kg per year.

eggs_per_hen.what: US commercial laying hens, 2011. Egg mass: no published AVERAGE found; US size class 'Large' has minimum mass 56.8 g per egg, Medium 49.6 g (Wikipedia Chicken egg sizes table). OWID egg yield per bird 2024: USA 17.26 kg/bird/yr, World 11.29 kg/bird/yr (grapher egg-yield-per-bird); 17.26 kg / 330 eggs would imply ~52 g but that mixes years and sources.
eggs_per_hen.quote: For hens used in egg production in the US, as of 2011 the FCR was about 2, with each hen laying about 330 eggs per year.
eggs_per_hen.egg_mass_quote: Large (L) | 56.8 g | 2 oz. ; Medium (M) | 49.6 g | 1.75 oz.

water_pigs.what: Feeder pig 70-110 kg: requirement range 7.3-10, typical 9 L/day (23-36 kg: 3.2-4.5; lactating sow 18.1-22.7). Ontario OMAFRA Factsheet 07-023 'Water Requirements of Livestock' (archived copy). Drinking water.
water_pigs.quote: Table 3. Water Consumption by Swine: Feeder pig | 70-110 | 7.3-10 | 9 ... 'five hundred 23-kg (50-lb) pigs at the start of a growout cycle will each consume 4.5 L/day. By the end of the growout cycle, the water requirements of these same 500 pigs, now weighing 100 kg (220 lb), will have doubled to 9 L/day each.'

water_cattle.what: Feedlot beef cattle 364-636 kg: range 27-55, typical 41 L/day (backgrounder 181-364 kg: 15-40, typical 25; lactating cows with calves 43-67). Ontario OMAFRA Factsheet 07-023 'Water Requirements of Livestock' (archived copy). Drinking water.
water_cattle.quote: Table 2. Water Consumption by Beef Cattle: Feedlot cattle: Short keep | 364-636 (800-1,400 lb) | 27-55 | 41

water_dairy_cow.what: Milking cows: 68-83 L/day at 13.6 kg milk/day up to 132-155 at 45.5 kg milk/day; average typical 115 L/day; dry cows 34-49. Ontario OMAFRA Factsheet 07-023 'Water Requirements of Livestock' (archived copy). Drinking water.
water_dairy_cow.quote: Table 1. Water Consumption by Dairy Cattle: Milking cows | 13.6 | 68-83 | 115 ; Milking cows | 36.3 | 114-136 | 115 ; Milking cows | 45.5 | 132-155 | 115 ; Dry cows | - | 34-49 | 41

water_sheep.what: Feeder lamb 27-50 kg: 3.6-5.2, typical 4.4 L/day (gestating meat ewe 4.0-6.5; lactating ewe with lambs 9.0-10.5). Ontario OMAFRA Factsheet 07-023 'Water Requirements of Livestock' (archived copy). Drinking water.
water_sheep.quote: Table 5. Water Consumption by Sheep: Feeder lamb | 27-50 | 3.6-5.2 | 4.4 ; Gestating meat ewe/ram | 80 | 4.0-6.5 | 5.25 ; Lactating meat ewe plus unweaned offspring | 80+ | 9.0-10.5 | 10

water_poultry.what: Typical annual-average: laying hens 250 L per 1,000 birds/day (range 180-320) = 0.25 L/bird; broilers 280 L per 1,000 birds/day (summer 450) = 0.28 L/bird; broilers by age at 21 C: 50-260 (weeks 1-4), 345-470 (weeks 5-8) L/1,000 birds/day. Layers ~4 kg water per dozen eggs. Ontario OMAFRA Factsheet 07-023 'Water Requirements of Livestock' (archived copy). Drinking water.
water_poultry.quote: Table 7: Winter, fall, spring | 280 ; Summer | 450 (L/1,000 birds/day). Table 8: Laying hens | 1.6-1.9 | 180-320 | 250. 'It has been estimated that laying hens will drink about 4 kg of water per dozen eggs produced.'

pig_slaughter_weight.what: US hog slaughter weight 270-285 lb (converted at 0.4536 kg/lb), reached in 22-26 weeks from birth. USDA ERS.
pig_slaughter_weight.quote: Farrow-to-finish operations raise hogs from birth to slaughter weight, about 270–285 pounds. [...] In a farrow-to-finish operation, 22–26 weeks (or about 6 months, starting at birth) are required to grow a pig to slaughter weight.

broiler_slaughter_weight.what: US average broiler market liveweight 2025: 6.63 lb (converted). Europe-style lighter bird: 'about 2 kg in only 5 to 7 weeks' (Wikipedia Broiler).
broiler_slaughter_weight.quote: 2025 47.5 6.63 1.70 5.95 (Market Age average days / Market Weight pounds, liveweight / feed per lb liveweight / mortality %)

broiler_cycle_days.what: US average broiler market age 2025 (at 6.63 lb / 3.0 kg). Wikipedia Broiler: slaughter-weight of about 2 kg in 5 to 7 weeks.

dressing_beef.what: Carcass weight as % of liveweight, grain-fed beef (grass-fed 56-58). SDSU: 62-64% for fed beef; Penn State: 63% average.
dressing_beef.quote: Table 1. Average dressing percentages for the four major livestock species: Beef (grain-fed) 60 – 63; Beef (grass-fed) 56 – 58; Pork (skin-on) 70 – 73; Sheep (shorn) 50 – 53; Goat 45 – 50

dressing_pork.what: Carcass (skin-on) as % of liveweight. Oklahoma brochure: 250 lb hog -> 180 lb dressed (72%).

dressing_lamb.what: Carcass as % of liveweight, shorn sheep.

dressing_chicken.what: Dressed weight of chickens and other fowl (skin on, feathers off) as % of liveweight. Wikipedia article (flagged 'more citations needed').
dressing_chicken.quote: the dress weight for chickens and other fowl is closer to 75% of the live weight, which is significantly higher than that of cattle, which can be from 50-70% depending on breed and methods used.

meat_yield_beef.what: Boneless trimmed beef (steaks, roasts, lean trim) from a 750 lb carcass of a 1,200 lb steer: 490 lb = 65% of carcass, = 41% of liveweight (490/1200, my arithmetic). Range of retail yield 55-75% of carcass.
meat_yield_beef.quote: A typical 750 carcass with ½ inch of fat over the rib eye and average muscling of a 12-13 square inch rib eye will yield about 65% of the carcass weight as retail cuts (roasts and steaks) and lean trim. [...] A 1200 steer, ½ inch fat, average muscling, yields a 750 pound carcass. The 750 pound carcass yields approximately: 490 pounds boneless trimmed beef; 150 pounds fat trim; 110 pounds bone

meat_yield_pork.what: Retail cuts (mixed bone-in and boneless, includes feet/head/back fat lines in the brochure) from a 250 lb hog: 144 lb = 57% of live, 80% of the 180 lb carcass. NOT strictly boneless. Oklahoma Dept. of Agriculture 'How Much Meat?' (archived).
meat_yield_pork.quote: On average about 57% of a hog make it from the pen to the pan. A 250 lb. hog will yield approximately 144 lbs of retail cuts. Around 28% of a hog's live weight is inedible product removed during the slaughter and dressing procedure bringing our 250 lb. live hog to 180 lbs. dressed. [...] another 20% of the weight is removed bringing our 180 lb. carcass to 144 lbs. of retail cuts.

meat_yield_lamb.what: BONE-IN chops and roasts plus ground lamb: 46 lb from a '120-pound lamb' = 38% (my arithmetic). CAVEAT: the table title says '120-pound lamb carcass' but the sister tables ('1,200-pound beef carcass', '250-pound pig carcass') are clearly live weights, so this is most likely % of LIVEWEIGHT; the table's own source line reads 'SOURCE?'. Low confidence; no boneless lamb figure found.
meat_yield_lamb.quote: Table 4. Average amount of meat from a 120-pound lamb carcass. Bone-in chops and roasts, shorn fleece | Shorn | 80 | 20 | 46 [approx. amt. of freezer meat (lb)] ... SOURCE? Note: Estimations may vary.

fillet_yield_fish.what: Skinless fillet as % of whole fish, FAO Fisheries Technical Paper 309 Table 1: Atlantic cod 34, Alaska pollack 36, common carp 36, tilapias [37], Pacific salmon (chum/coho/pink/sockeye) [50]. Square brackets = provisional values in the source. Total edible flesh: cod 47, pollack 41, salmon 62.
fillet_yield_fish.quote: Species | Yield (as % of whole fish or shellfish weight) Skinless Fillet | Edible Flesh ...: Alaska pollack 36 41 ; Atlantic cod 34 47 ; Common carp 36 [54] ; Tilapias nei [37] 37 ; Chum salmon (13) [50] 62

manure_pigs.unit: kg fresh manure per head per day
manure_pigs.what: Grow-finish pig, 150 lb (68 kg) average weight: 9.5 lb/day. Ohio State Univ. Extension Bulletin 604, Table 1 'Fresh Manure Production and Characteristics per Animal Type' (adapted from MWPS-18); table is in lb/day, converted here at 0.4536 kg/lb. Fresh manure = faeces + urine.

manure_dairy_cow.unit: kg fresh manure per head per day
manure_dairy_cow.what: Lactating cow 1,400 lb (635 kg): 128 lb/day at 50 lb milk/day, 153 lb/day at 90 lb milk/day. Ohio State Univ. Extension Bulletin 604, Table 1 'Fresh Manure Production and Characteristics per Animal Type' (adapted from MWPS-18); table is in lb/day, converted here at 0.4536 kg/lb. Fresh manure = faeces + urine.

manure_beef.unit: kg fresh manure per head per day
manure_beef.what: Beef cattle on high-energy (feedlot) ration, 1,100 lb (499 kg): 80 lb/day; high-forage 1,100 lb: 92 lb/day (42 kg). Ohio State Univ. Extension Bulletin 604, Table 1 'Fresh Manure Production and Characteristics per Animal Type' (adapted from MWPS-18); table is in lb/day, converted here at 0.4536 kg/lb. Fresh manure = faeces + urine.

manure_layers.unit: kg fresh manure per bird per day
manure_layers.what: Layer, 4 lb (1.8 kg) bird: 0.26 lb/day. Ohio State Univ. Extension Bulletin 604, Table 1 'Fresh Manure Production and Characteristics per Animal Type' (adapted from MWPS-18); table is in lb/day, converted here at 0.4536 kg/lb. Fresh manure = faeces + urine.

manure_broilers.unit: kg fresh manure per bird per day
manure_broilers.what: Broiler, 2 lb (0.9 kg) average bird: 0.18 lb/day. Ohio State Univ. Extension Bulletin 604, Table 1 'Fresh Manure Production and Characteristics per Animal Type' (adapted from MWPS-18); table is in lb/day, converted here at 0.4536 kg/lb. Fresh manure = faeces + urine.

flour_extraction.what: White (roller-milled) flour extraction rate: about 72% or less of the whole grain. Kansas Wheat: a 60 lb bushel yields ~42 lb white flour (70%).
flour_extraction.quote: extracting about 72% of the whole grain kernel [...] This lower extraction (typically 72% or less) is most commonly Roller Milled White Enriched Flour

oil_content_rapeseed.what: Oil content of canola/rapeseed seed; crushing yield 10 L oil (about 9.2 kg at 0.92 g/ml) from 23 kg seed = ~40% by mass. Feedipedia: 46% of DM (40-50%).
oil_content_rapeseed.quote: About 44% of a seed is oil, with the remainder as a canola meal used for animal feed. About 23 kg of canola seed makes 10 litre of canola oil.

oil_content_sunflower.what: Oil-type sunflower seeds (whole, with hull; hull = 20% of seed); confectionery types 30%. Same page: oil is 'about 50% of the seed dry weight'.
oil_content_sunflower.quote: Oil type seeds contain 40% oil and represent 80-95% of sunflower seed production. The hulls (20% of the seed) are black and tend to adhere to the kernels (USDA, 2010).

oil_content_soybean.what: Oil content of soybean seed (same article elsewhere: 'approximately 20%').
oil_content_soybean.quote: Soybean seed contains 18–19% oil. To extract soybean oil from seed, the soybeans are cracked, adjusted for moisture content, rolled into flakes, and solvent-extracted

sugar_from_beet.unit: kg sugar per tonne of beet
sugar_from_beet.what: Sugar obtained per tonne of sugar beet roots (plus 500 kg wet pulp). Beet sugar content 12-21%, about 20% typical (Wikipedia Sugar beet).
sugar_from_beet.quote: It has been reported that 1 ton of sugarbeets yields approximately 150 kg of sugar and 500 kg of wet beet pulp (or 210 kg pressed beet pulp, or 50 kg dehydrated beet pulp) (Legrand, 2015).

sugar_from_cane.unit: kg sucrose per tonne of clean cane stalk
sugar_from_cane.what: SUCROSE CONTAINED in one tonne of burned-and-cropped cane stalk (Brazil), not recovered white sugar; recovery would be lower. Same article: mature stalk is 12-16% soluble sugars.
sugar_from_cane.quote: Each ton of b&c yields 740 kg of juice (135 kg of sucrose and 605 kg of water) and 260 kg of moist bagasse (130 kg of dry bagasse).

cheese_yield.what: Grana Padano (hard, long-aged cheese). Parmesan article: 1,100 L milk per vat makes two wheels of ~45 kg fresh curd each. No figure found for Cheddar.
cheese_yield.quote: About 14.4 kg of milk yield 1 kg of cheese.

butter_yield.what: Theoretical yield worked example, University of Guelph Dairy Science and Technology eBook: 100 kg of 3.6% fat milk -> 8.9 kg of 40% cream -> 4.35 kg butter (81.5% fat), i.e. 100/4.35 = 23 kg milk per kg butter (my division).
butter_yield.quote: If 100 kg of milk was used, 8.9 kg of cream would be produced (from a Pearson Square mass balance) and 4.35 kg butter would be produced from that. This is the theoretical yield based on no losses.

bread_yield.what: US commercial white bread: 16 oz flour in a 24 oz loaf = 1.5 (my division). Same page: a bushel (42 lb white flour) makes 42 one-and-a-half pound loaves.
bread_yield.quote: There are approximately 16 ounces of flour in a one-and-a-half pound loaf of bread. [...] A bushel of wheat yields 42 commercial loaves of white bread (one-and-a-half pound loaves).

beer_malt.unit: kg malt per hectolitre of beer
beer_malt.what: Maltsters' Association of Great Britain: 1 tonne malt -> 8,837 L beer, i.e. 1000/88.37 = 11.3 kg malt/hl (my division); 1.3 t barley per t malt -> about 14.7 kg barley/hl.
beer_malt.quote: 1.3 tonne of barley makes 1 tonne of malt; 1 tonne of malt makes 54 barrels of beer; 1 barrel of beer = 163.65 litres; 54 barrels = 8,837 litres

wine_yield.unit: kg grapes per litre of wine
wine_yield.what: Grapes needed per litre: 1.6 kg white, 1.3 kg red, 1.4 kg mixed (= 625 / 770 / 715 L wine per tonne of grapes, my conversion).
wine_yield.quote: Representative figures for the amount of grapes needed for 100 L of wine are 160 kg for white wine, 130 kg for red wine, and 140 kg for a mixture of red and white wine.

ammonia_energy.what: Haber-Bosch incl. feedstock energy: best available technology 28 GJ/t (natural gas), 36 GJ/t (coal); global average today ~41 GJ/t net. IEA Ammonia Technology Roadmap executive summary (archived). Royal Society 2020 briefing: conventional production consumes '8 MWh of energy per tonne of ammonia' (28.8 GJ/t). No published electrolysis-route figure was read.
ammonia_energy.quote: The global average energy intensity of ammonia production today is around 41 GJ/t on a net basis, compared with best available technology (BAT) energy performance levels of 28 GJ/t for natural gas-based production and 36 GJ/t for coal-based production.
ammonia_energy.second_quote: Overall, brown ammonia production is energy intensive, consuming 8 MWh of energy per tonne of ammonia.

fertiliser_n_rate.unit: kg N per ha of cropland per year
fertiliser_n_rate.what: World average nitrogen fertiliser use per hectare of cropland, 2023 (FAO data via OWID). Same file 2023: USA 59.08, Netherlands 90.56, Denmark 81.86. Not crop-specific.
fertiliser_n_rate.quote: CSV row: World,OWID_WRL,2023,67.72 (column: nutrient nitrogen N (total), use per area of cropland, kilograms per hectare)

notes: All entries were read from the fetched page text (curl), none from search excerpts; the web-search tool was unavailable (session budget exhausted), so sources are pages reachable by known URL: fewer primary sources than ideal, several via Wikipedia.

Partial gaps inside found items: ammonia_energy has no electrolysis-route figure; eggs_per_hen has no true average egg mass (size-class minimum only); sugar_from_cane is sucrose content, not recovered sugar; cheese_yield is Grana Padano only; meat_yield_pork and meat_yield_lamb are not strictly boneless; fcr_beef/fcr_pigs sources do not state dry-matter basis; feed_per_kg_milk dry-matter basis not printed in the CSV.
Values marked 'my arithmetic/division/conversion' are unit conversions or ratios of the quoted figures, not printed in the source.
Quotes from Wikipedia have wiki markup and reference tags removed; table rows are flattened text.
